{\LARGE\bfseries\sffamily\color{AtlasNavy} Convex optimization with Hölder-continuous gradients and exact values\par}\vspace{5pt}
\textbf{Setting ID.} \texttt{SO\_\allowbreak{}\allowbreak{}ZO\_\allowbreak{}\allowbreak{}E07\_\allowbreak{}\allowbreak{}neighborhood}

Single-objective optimization

Minimize \AtlasInlineMath{f} globally over \AtlasInlineMath{B_2(0,R)} and return a point with small objective gap.

\textbf{Status.} Polynomial gap present

\textbf{TASK tags.} formulation: Global minimization; solution concept: Global minimization; task family: Single objective

\textbf{MODEL tags.} convexity: Convex; smoothness: Gradient holder; structure: No additional structure

\textbf{ORACLE tags.} access order: Zeroth-order interface; interface family: Exact value; public information: Public inputs explicitly declared; operation: Function value; feedback quality: Exact

\textbf{ALGORITHMS tags.} adaptivity: Adaptive; randomization: Deterministic algorithms; randomization: Private randomness allowed; restriction: No additional span restriction explicitly imposed

\textbf{OUTPUT tags.} certificate: No additional output certificate required

\textbf{METRIC tags.} criterion: Objective gap

\textbf{GUARANTEE tags.} aggregation: Per instance; mode: Deterministic; mode: Probability

\textbf{RESOURCE tags.} budget: Fixed worst-case budget

\needspace{7\baselineskip}\section{1. Setting specification}
\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Task}
Minimize \AtlasInlineMath{f} globally over \AtlasInlineMath{B_2(0,R)} and return a point with small objective gap.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Admissible model}
\AtlasInlineMath{f} is convex and continuously differentiable on an open neighborhood of \AtlasInlineMath{B_2(0,R+\tau)}, with \AtlasInlineMath{\tau>0}. For every \AtlasInlineMath{x,y} in this neighborhood, \AtlasInlineMath{\|\nabla f(x)-\nabla f(y)\|_2\le H_\nu\|x-y\|_2^\nu}, where \AtlasInlineMath{0<\nu<1}.

Minimize over \AtlasInlineMath{B_2(0,R)}, allowing boundary optima. The neighborhood thickness is part of the query permission; a function defined in the ball is not automatically extended to the ambient space.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Oracle interface}
At any finite query point \AtlasInlineMath{x} in \AtlasInlineMath{B_2(0,R+\tau)}, the oracle returns the single exact scalar \AtlasInlineMath{f(x)}. The reply is uniquely determined and contains no gradient, subgradient or derivative-vector product.

Projection and the stated proximal operations over known geometry are free.

The public inputs are \AtlasInlineMath{d}, \AtlasInlineMath{\nu}, \AtlasInlineMath{H_\nu}, \AtlasInlineMath{R}, \AtlasInlineMath{\tau}, \AtlasInlineMath{\varepsilon}, together with the sets, kernels and auxiliary operations explicitly declared above. Information about the unknown objective and any undisclosed sample distribution is obtained only through the stated interface.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Output}
Return \AtlasInlineMath{\widehat{x}\in B_2(0,R)}. The output may be an unqueried point, an average or convex combination that remains in the stated space. No function value, gradient, inner solution, or accuracy certificate must accompany the output.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Loss or accuracy criterion}
The base loss is \AtlasInlineMath{\ell(I,x)=f(x)-f_*}, where \AtlasInlineMath{f_*=\inf_{u\in B_2(0,R)}f(u)}. This nonnegative loss is evaluated at the output, with tolerance \AtlasInlineMath{\varepsilon}.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Resource accounting}
Each scalar function value or noisy observation costs \AtlasInlineMath{1} call. Every location in a multipoint finite difference, every initialization query, and every reference observation is charged.

Only the declared oracle resource is charged. Computation and storage using existing information, together with explicitly known geometric and proximal operations, are free.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Algorithm views and success guarantees}
\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsubsection{Deterministic}
Only deterministic strategies are allowed. Queries, stopping and postprocessing may be arbitrary measurable adaptive functions of the history. No linear-span or zero-respecting restriction is imposed.

Interactions are sequential, and every actual response in a batch is charged separately. Except for explicitly listed auxiliary interfaces, arithmetic, linear algebra, storage, and internal computation on available information are free, with no additional communication or memory restriction. Finite-difference steps must be finite and positive; real-number precision is not charged separately.

After fixing the public inputs, choose one algorithm that works for every admissible instance and reply law. The requirement \AtlasInlineMath{\ell(I,\widehat{x})\le \varepsilon} holds deterministically for each instance.

Oracle cost uses a deterministic worst-case budget: \AtlasInlineMath{N\le T} on every possible execution path. For multiple resources, coordinatewise caps apply jointly along the same path.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsubsection{Randomized}
Private randomization is allowed, with the seed independent of the instance and external randomness. Queries, stopping and postprocessing may be arbitrary measurable adaptive functions of the history. No linear-span or zero-respecting restriction is imposed.

Interactions are sequential, and every actual response in a batch is charged separately. Except for explicitly listed auxiliary interfaces, arithmetic, linear algebra, storage, and internal computation on available information are free, with no additional communication or memory restriction. Finite-difference steps must be finite and positive; real-number precision is not charged separately.

After fixing the public inputs, choose one algorithm that works for every admissible instance and reply law. The error requirement is \AtlasInlineMath{\Pr(\ell(I,\widehat{x})\le \varepsilon)\ge2/3}.

Probability is over the algorithm's random seed only.

Oracle cost uses a deterministic worst-case budget: \AtlasInlineMath{N\le T} on every possible execution path. For multiple resources, coordinatewise caps apply jointly along the same path.

\textbf{Output qualification.} Random selection among previously queried points is permitted, subject to the declared success guarantee.

\needspace{7\baselineskip}\section{2. Notation and parameters}
\AtlasInlineMath{d}: Dimension of the variable space \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{d\in\mathbb{N},\ d\ge1}.

\AtlasInlineMath{\nu}: Gradient Hölder exponent \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{0<\nu<1}.

\AtlasInlineMath{H_\nu}: Gradient Hölder modulus \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{H_\nu>0}.

\AtlasInlineMath{\|\nabla f(x)-\nabla f(y)\|_2\le H_\nu\|x-y\|_2^\nu}

\AtlasInlineMath{R}: Feasible-ball radius \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{R>0}.

The output must belong to \AtlasInlineMath{B_2(0,R)}; the query radius is specified separately in the interface.

\AtlasInlineMath{\tau}: Thickness of the queryable neighborhood outside the ball \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\tau>0}.

The query domain is \AtlasInlineMath{B_2(0,R+\tau)}.

\AtlasInlineMath{\varepsilon}: Error target; norm and squared-norm criteria use different thresholds \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\varepsilon>0}.

\AtlasInlineMath{W}: Accuracy ratio for Hölder-continuous gradients \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{W>0}.

\AtlasInlineMath{W=H_\nu R^{1+\nu}/\varepsilon}

\AtlasInlineMath{C_\nu}: Dimension or accuracy constant depending only on the fixed Hölder exponent \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{C_\nu>0}.

Determined by the applicable theorem conditions; retain a symbolic threshold when no numerical value is supplied.

\AtlasInlineMath{W_{0,\nu}}: Accuracy threshold depending only on the fixed Hölder exponent \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{W_{0,\nu}>0}.

Determined by the applicable theorem conditions; retain a symbolic threshold when no numerical value is supplied.

\AtlasInlineMath{x,y,u}: Function arguments and dummy variables in the formulas \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{x,y,u\in\mathbb{R}^d}; spherical domains are embedded in \AtlasInlineMath{\mathbb{R}^{d+1}}.

Admissible ranges are specified separately by the task, model and oracle in this profile.

\AtlasInlineMath{\widehat{x}}: Final algorithm output \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{B_2(0,R)}.

\AtlasInlineMath{I}: Complete problem instance \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{I\in\mathcal{I}}.

Includes the unknown objective and its admissible feedback distribution or environment law. Public parameters are fixed before the quantifiers.

\AtlasInlineMath{\mathcal{I}}: Admissible instance class determined by the eight specification fields in this profile \textbf{Domain:} Instances satisfying the public parameter bounds.

\AtlasInlineMath{\mathcal{A}}: Algorithm or strategy \textbf{Domain:} Measurable adaptive strategies allowed in this profile.

The algorithm is selected before the hidden instance.

\AtlasInlineMath{\ell}: Base loss or residual \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\ell:\mathcal{I}\times\mathcal{X}_{\mathrm{out}}\to[0,+\infty]}.

The exact formula appears in this profile's performance-criterion section.

\AtlasInlineMath{\mathbb{E},\Pr}: Expectation and probability \textbf{Domain:} Evaluated over the algorithmic and feedback randomness specified by this profile's guarantee.

Fix the instance first; aggregate cost and error separately.

\AtlasInlineMath{\inf,\sup}: Infimum and supremum \textbf{Domain:} Evaluated only over the variable sets explicitly specified in the formula.

In the risk definition, the infimum over algorithms precedes the supremum over instances or centers.

\AtlasInlineMath{\|\cdot\|_2,\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle}: Euclidean norm and inner product \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\|x\|_2=\sqrt{\langle x,x\rangle}}.

\AtlasInlineMath{\langle x,y\rangle=x^\top y}

\AtlasInlineMath{B_p(c,R)}: Closed norm ball \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{p\in[1,\infty],\ R\ge0}.

\AtlasInlineMath{B_p(c,R)=\{x:\|x-c\|_p\le R\}}; \AtlasInlineMath{B_2} denotes the Euclidean ball.

\AtlasInlineMath{N,T}: Actual call count and declared budget \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{N,T\in\mathbb{N}_0}.

A fixed budget bounds every execution path; the Markov specification uses an expected budget.

\AtlasInlineMath{O,\Omega,\Theta,\widetilde{O}}: Asymptotic upper bounds, lower bounds, matching orders, and upper bounds with hidden logarithms \textbf{Domain:} Within the joint parameter window specified for each complexity regime.

Dependence of hidden constants on fixed parameters is stated separately for each bound. Tilde notation may hide logarithmic factors only in the declared variables.

\AtlasInlineMath{c,C,c_\alpha,C_\alpha}: Positive constant in a proof or asymptotic bound \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{0<c,C,c_\alpha,C_\alpha<\infty}.

Unsubscripted constants have the dependencies stated in the bound; constants subscripted by \AtlasInlineMath{\alpha} may depend only on the fixed smoothness order.

\AtlasInlineMath{\log,\log_+,e}: Natural logarithm, truncated logarithm, and Euler's number \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{z>0}.

\AtlasInlineMath{\log_+(z)=\max\{0,\log z\}}; \AtlasInlineMath{e=\exp(1)}, and \AtlasInlineMath{\log_2} denotes the base-two logarithm.

\AtlasInlineMath{f,f_*}: Population objective and its optimal value \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{f:\mathcal{X}_{\mathrm{fun}}\to\mathbb{R}}.

\AtlasInlineMath{f_*=\inf_{x\in B_2(0,R)}f(x)}.

\AtlasInlineMath{\nabla f,\nabla^2f,D^jf}: Gradient, Hessian, and higher Fréchet derivatives \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\nabla f\in\mathbb{R}^d,\ \nabla^2f\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}}; \AtlasInlineMath{D^jf} is a \AtlasInlineMath{j}-linear form.

Used only at derivative orders and on regions where the model guarantees its existence.

\AtlasInlineMath{\|\cdot\|_{\mathrm{op}}}: Euclidean induced matrix or tensor operator norm \textbf{Domain:} Take the supremum over Euclidean unit input vectors of the corresponding order.

\AtlasInlineMath{\|T\|_{\mathrm{op}}=\sup_{\|u_1\|_2,\ldots,\|u_j\|_2\le1}|T[u_1,\ldots,u_j]|}

\AtlasInlineMath{\mathcal{X}_{\mathrm{fun}},\mathcal{X}_{\mathrm{out}},\mathcal{X}}: Function domain, admissible output domain and optimization domain \textbf{Domain:} Each is the Euclidean space or subset explicitly specified in this profile.

\AtlasInlineMath{\mathcal{X}_{\mathrm{out}}=B_2(0,R)} and \AtlasInlineMath{\mathcal{X}=B_2(0,R)}; the function domain is the region on which the model imposes regularity.

\AtlasInlineMath{N^*}: Optimal worst-case oracle complexity satisfying the complete guarantee \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{N^*\in[0,+\infty]}.

Take the infimum over admissible algorithms, followed by the worst case over the instances of this profile. With multiple resources, use this scalar only for an explicitly specified resource projection.

\textbf{Direction.} upper

\textbf{Conditions.} \AtlasInlineMath{W=H_\nu R^{1+\nu}/\varepsilon\ge1}. This is a constructive upper bound, without a claim of zeroth-order optimality. The gradient approximation error is controlled by \AtlasInlineMath{h^\nu}.

\textbf{Oracle correspondence.} Exact scalar function values; every location required by a finite difference must belong to this setting's query domain.

\textbf{Guarantee conversion.} Error uses this profile's accuracy scale and aggregation order. The source theorem's expectation, probability, and asymptotic quantifiers are retained separately.

\textbf{Output rule.} The output need only lie in this setting's prescribed space. Permitted averages and unqueried outputs must still satisfy its feasibility conditions.

\textbf{Resource conversion.} Atomic calls under a fixed cap on every execution path. All feedback obtained during initialization, differencing and inner iterations is charged.

\textbf{Local argument.} ZO\_\allowbreak{}PROOF\_\allowbreak{}HOLDER

\textbf{Source location.} \href{https://optimization-online.org/wp-content/uploads/2013/04/3833.pdf}{[2]} theorem: Universal gradient method with finite-difference simulation

\begingroup\raggedright\sloppy Writing \$W=\allowbreak{}H\_\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}nu R\textasciicircum{}\{1+\textbackslash{}nu\}/\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}varepsilon\$,\allowbreak{} an upper is \$O\_\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}nu(d[1+W\textasciicircum{}\{2/\allowbreak{}(1+3\textbackslash{}nu)\}])\$. A lower \$\textbackslash{}Omega\_\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}nu(W\textasciicircum{}\{2/\allowbreak{}(1+3\textbackslash{}nu)\})\$ holds for \$W\textbackslash{}ge W\_\allowbreak{}\{0,\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}nu\}\$ and\newline{}\$\$d\textbackslash{}ge\textbackslash{}max\textbackslash{}\{8,\allowbreak{}C\_\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}nu W\textasciicircum{}\{8/\allowbreak{}(1+3\textbackslash{}nu)\}\textbackslash{}log(eW)\textbackslash{}\}.\$\$\newline{}\newline{}At any feasible point,\allowbreak{} forward differences with \$0<h\textbackslash{}le\textbackslash{}tau\$ satisfy \$\textbackslash{}|\textbackslash{}widehat g-\textbackslash{}nabla f(x)\textbackslash{}|\textbackslash{}le\textbackslash{}sqrt dH\_\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}nu h\textasciicircum{}\textbackslash{}nu/\allowbreak{}(1+\textbackslash{}nu)\$. Thus \$d+1\$ exact values achieve any prescribed positive gradient error. On a set of diameter \$2R\$,\allowbreak{} shifting the reported function value downward by \$2R\textbackslash{}eta\$ gives a valid lower first-order model. The upper model error is at most \$4R\textbackslash{}eta+H\_\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}nu\textbackslash{}|y-x\textbackslash{}|\textasciicircum{}\{1+\textbackslash{}nu\}/\allowbreak{}(1+\textbackslash{}nu)\$. Young's inequality bounds the latter by \$M\_\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}delta\textbackslash{}|y-x\textbackslash{}|\textasciicircum{}2/\allowbreak{}2+\textbackslash{}delta/\allowbreak{}2\$,\allowbreak{} where \$M\_\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}delta=\allowbreak{}C\_\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}nu H\_\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}nu\textasciicircum{}\{2/\allowbreak{}(1+\textbackslash{}nu)\}\textbackslash{}delta\textasciicircum{}\{-(1-\textbackslash{}nu)/\allowbreak{}(1+\textbackslash{}nu)\}\$. Choose \$\textbackslash{}eta\textbackslash{}le\textbackslash{}delta/\allowbreak{}(8R)\$. The universal inexact accelerated model bound is \$O(M\_\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}delta R\textasciicircum{}2/\allowbreak{}N\textasciicircum{}2+N\textbackslash{}delta)\$. Taking \$\textbackslash{}delta\$ a small multiple of \$\textbackslash{}varepsilon/\allowbreak{}N\$ and solving yields the stated iteration count,\allowbreak{} multiplied by \$O(d)\$ values. The additive one is needed because unrestricted affine terms remain legal even if \$H\_\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}nu\$ is tiny.\newline{}\newline{}For the lower use Diakonikolas and Guzman,\allowbreak{} Theorem 12,\allowbreak{} at norm \$p=\allowbreak{}2\$ and parallel batch size one. Its two terms scale as \$W\textasciicircum{}\{2/\allowbreak{}(1+3\textbackslash{}nu)\}\$ and \$dW\textasciicircum{}\{-6/\allowbreak{}(1+3\textbackslash{}nu)\}/\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}log M\$. Choose \$M\$ a small constant multiple of the first term. The displayed dimension makes the second no smaller than the first. The radial shielding in the source construction handles exterior queries,\allowbreak{} and its ball-contained witness preserves the constrained optimum comparison. If the target returns an unqueried feasible point,\allowbreak{} append one query there to meet the source's successful-query convention;\allowbreak{} the \$W\textbackslash{}ge W\_\allowbreak{}\{0,\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}nu\}\$ condition absorbs that one call. Scale coordinates by \$R\$ and values by \$H\_\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}nu R\textasciicircum{}\{1+\textbackslash{}nu\}\$. The source lower concerns a stronger local first-order oracle and so also limits exact-value algorithms,\allowbreak{} without acquiring an extra factor of \$d\$.\par\endgroup

\begingroup\raggedright\sloppy Retained premises,\allowbreak{} not historical recertification:\allowbreak{} /\allowbreak{}common\_\allowbreak{}specification @ cb48cb4b4baea9df2c2680eec34eefd13baf4283f8883190d24fe490f128f366 supplies the Euclidean feasible/\allowbreak{}output ball of radius R,\allowbreak{} scalar exact-value oracle,\allowbreak{} fixed-path query cost,\allowbreak{} and the gradient seminorm inequality <=\allowbreak{}H\_\allowbreak{}nu on the query neighborhood. /\allowbreak{}views @ 2f0a5ec56525ede164a1e741b632b782e6e1d6a60694e8420371420f75b33245 supplies arbitrary measurable adaptive deterministic algorithms and private-random algorithms with per-instance success >=\allowbreak{}2/\allowbreak{}3. /\allowbreak{}resource\_\allowbreak{}projections/\allowbreak{}0 @ 51e8191c0794f51712b73e70c0665ecc79d2490f05e1d9dd0bc91c93dd6879de fixes one value per call. The q1 minimax quantities are /\allowbreak{}quantities/\allowbreak{}0 @ 8f04168525f60569d0129c9d52a55c82fcf0e8406645a6e3ddf554667b400cea and /\allowbreak{}quantities/\allowbreak{}2 @ 98a48d9e22187046a9e92061ea4f10395029a666bb1545cf6c39f1085961c6f5. No external theorem is used below.\newline{}\newline{}I. Subclass and preservation. Every f(x)=\allowbreak{}a.x+b,\allowbreak{} with arbitrary a in R\textasciicircum{}d and b in R,\allowbreak{} is globally convex C1 and has gradient Holder seminorm zero,\allowbreak{} hence belongs for every permitted positive H\_\allowbreak{}nu and every tau>0. Its constrained minimum is b-R||a||. Each permitted value is the single scalar a.q+b;\allowbreak{} neither an unqueried output nor free postprocessing yields an additional observation. The subclass retains the original query domain,\allowbreak{} output ball,\allowbreak{} guarantees and fixed path caps;\allowbreak{} it does not impose an affine promise on the target.\newline{}\newline{}II. Exact deterministic lower. Suppose a deterministic algorithm has cap k<=\allowbreak{}d and run it on the admissible zero function. Let q\_\allowbreak{}1,\allowbreak{}...,\allowbreak{}q\_\allowbreak{}m,\allowbreak{} m<=\allowbreak{}k,\allowbreak{} be its actual queries and y its feasible output. If m>=\allowbreak{}1 the m homogeneous equations a.q\_\allowbreak{}i+b=\allowbreak{}0 in d+1 unknowns admit a nonzero solution (a,\allowbreak{}b),\allowbreak{} necessarily with a!=\allowbreak{}0 because a=\allowbreak{}0 would force b=\allowbreak{}0. Choose sign sigma with sigma a.y>=\allowbreak{}0 and lambda>epsilon/\allowbreak{}(R||a||). The fixed instance f(x)=\allowbreak{}sigma lambda(a.x+b) reproduces every response and therefore the entire adaptive transcript and output. Its gap is lambda(sigma a.y+R||a||)>epsilon,\allowbreak{} a contradiction. If m=\allowbreak{}0 choose any nonzero a,\allowbreak{} choose its sign similarly,\allowbreak{} and scale;\allowbreak{} no response constraints are needed. Thus T\_\allowbreak{}det>=\allowbreak{}d+1 exactly,\allowbreak{} including d=\allowbreak{}1.\newline{}\newline{}III. Exact randomized lower. Let an algorithm have integer cap k. If k>=\allowbreak{}d,\allowbreak{} k>=\allowbreak{}d/\allowbreak{}9 is immediate;\allowbreak{} assume k<d. For each L>0 choose a uniformly on the radius-L sphere,\allowbreak{} independently of its private random tape,\allowbreak{} and consider f\_\allowbreak{}a(x)=\allowbreak{}a.x. Fix the tape. Construct an augmented transcript with one new orthogonal linear measurement at each of k steps. Maintain the span of previous augmented directions. If the algorithm's next actual query q has a nonzero orthogonal component,\allowbreak{} measure along that component's unit direction and reconstruct a.q from that answer and the already measured projection. If q lies in the span its answer is already determined,\allowbreak{} so measure any measurably selected orthogonal unit direction instead. After the algorithm stops,\allowbreak{} pad to k steps in the same way. Each such unit-direction measurement can be obtained at (R+tau) times the direction and divided by R+tau,\allowbreak{} using one permitted scalar value. Only the reconstructed original answers are shown to the original algorithm. Its output Y is therefore measurable in the enlarged history. This construction also handles dependent queries and data-dependent stopping.\newline{}\newline{}Conditional on the enlarged history after j measurements and the fixed tape,\allowbreak{} write a=\allowbreak{}p\_\allowbreak{}j+z\_\allowbreak{}j. Rotational symmetry shows inductively that z\_\allowbreak{}j is uniform on the sphere of radius sqrt(L\textasciicircum{}2-||p\_\allowbreak{}j||\textasciicircum{}2) in the (d-j)-dimensional orthogonal complement:\allowbreak{} a new predictable orthogonal direction fixes exactly its one coordinate and leaves a uniform orthogonal residual. Consequently E[a|history]=\allowbreak{}p\_\allowbreak{}j and the next squared-coordinate conditional mean is (L\textasciicircum{}2-||p\_\allowbreak{}j||\textasciicircum{}2)/\allowbreak{}(d-j). Starting at p\_\allowbreak{}0=\allowbreak{}0,\allowbreak{} the recursion gives E||p\_\allowbreak{}j||\textasciicircum{}2=\allowbreak{}jL\textasciicircum{}2/\allowbreak{}d. This proves the needed adaptive measurement statement directly,\allowbreak{} without an external information theorem.\newline{}\newline{}Average also over the private tape. The gap Z=\allowbreak{}RL+a.Y lies in [0,\allowbreak{}2RL] and E Z=\allowbreak{}RL+E[p\_\allowbreak{}k.Y]>=\allowbreak{}RL-R E||p\_\allowbreak{}k||>=\allowbreak{}RL(1-sqrt(k/\allowbreak{}d)). Uniform per-instance success >=\allowbreak{}2/\allowbreak{}3,\allowbreak{} integrated over the sphere,\allowbreak{} gives Pr(Z<=\allowbreak{}epsilon)>=\allowbreak{}2/\allowbreak{}3. For 2RL>epsilon this implies E Z<=\allowbreak{}2epsilon/\allowbreak{}3+2RL/\allowbreak{}3. Hence sqrt(k/\allowbreak{}d)>=\allowbreak{}1/\allowbreak{}3-2epsilon/\allowbreak{}(3RL). The fixed algorithm must satisfy this for every L,\allowbreak{} since slopes have no magnitude bound. Letting L tend to infinity gives k>=\allowbreak{}d/\allowbreak{}9 and therefore T\_\allowbreak{}rand>=\allowbreak{}ceil(d/\allowbreak{}9) exactly. The constructed instances are fixed before the random tape,\allowbreak{} so the adversarial-instance quantifier is preserved.\newline{}\newline{}IV. Envelope and endpoints. Retain b3/\allowbreak{}b4 only on their existing contracts and guards:\allowbreak{} /\allowbreak{}bounds @ d65950486a96732b19558449b3ee25c31c49fc99c9517c50c71e028cf1aff836,\allowbreak{} /\allowbreak{}comparisons @ 6a65a84e8fa068c8ece09c60f2732e04941a530a00704f718a33a858fc633ab6,\allowbreak{} and ZO\_\allowbreak{}PROOF\_\allowbreak{}HOLDER /\allowbreak{}proofs/\allowbreak{}0 @ 8e9b2cccbdd9204cd27a869418c0a80b7c7d0eace21574f0af7378874d978538. Combining either dimension lower with its view's b4 gives Omega\_\allowbreak{}nu(max\{d,\allowbreak{}W\textasciicircum{}(2/\allowbreak{}(1+3nu))\}) on the existing high-dimensional guard. The upper remains O\_\allowbreak{}nu(d W\textasciicircum{}(2/\allowbreak{}(1+3nu))) there;\allowbreak{} the additive one in b3 is absorbed because W>=\allowbreak{}W\_\allowbreak{}\{0,\allowbreak{}nu\}>0 with nu fixed. Taking their ratio gives O\_\allowbreak{}nu(min\{d,\allowbreak{}W\textasciicircum{}(2/\allowbreak{}(1+3nu))\}). For W>=\allowbreak{}1 the dimension condition implies W\textasciicircum{}(2/\allowbreak{}(1+3nu))<=\allowbreak{}C\_\allowbreak{}nu\textasciicircum{}(-1/\allowbreak{}4)d\textasciicircum{}(1/\allowbreak{}4);\allowbreak{} for W<1 it is <=\allowbreak{}1<=\allowbreak{}d. Thus on the guarded family the new lower is equivalently Omega\_\allowbreak{}nu(d),\allowbreak{} without asserting an exact crossover constant.
